environment.isolation: one monitored child process per measurement

compilerAudit.baseline: generic CompactGameProvider dispatch with repeated linear level lookup, transition revalidation and string-heavy synthetic utility/chance generation
dominantCosts: terminal history token arrays and string splitting
linear level scan repeated across provider methods
per-node labels and small temporary arrays
compilerAudit.optimized: level-sequential direct synthetic compilation into exact preallocated typed arrays with bounded chunk execution

cacheExperiment.coldMeaning: fresh isolated process; operating-system page cache was not forcibly purged

rustExperiment.scope: synthetic topology compilation and binary export only

H1.evidence: Removing repeated provider dispatch, linear level lookup and string-heavy per-node work produced a 2.33x-2.92x cold-compile speedup.

H2.evidence: All chunk sizes preserved the exact structural hash and bounded cancellation checks; peak RSS did not materially improve because storage is still exactly preallocated.

H3.evidence: Both the 6.10 baseline and V2 already preallocate exact typed-array capacity; no honest dynamic-growth counterfactual exists for the exactly sized synthetic provider.

H4.evidence: S5 validated cache load was 22.94x faster than baseline cold compilation.

H5.evidence: Full Rust integration took 2.52 times the optimized TypeScript time on S5.

H6.evidence: The decision uses full native process plus binary transfer, validation and TypeScript reconstruction time.

H7.evidence: S0-S5 compare exact integer topology arrays plus explicit 1e-12 floating-point tolerance.

rustDecision.recommendedArchitecture: Optimized TypeScript Compiler V2 for cache misses plus Structural Cache V1 for repeated games; retain the Rust CLI as an experimental differential oracle.
rustDecision.rationale: The classification is derived from the S5 end-to-end ratio 2.521 and cross-language equivalence=true.

limitations: The compiler optimization applies to the synthetic compact provider, not arbitrary poker trees.
Fresh-process cache timing does not guarantee a cold operating-system disk cache.
Rust is experimental and does not implement CFR, evaluation, checkpointing, or poker strategy.
Gate D remains FAIL and verified datasets remain zero.
